classification.difficultyReason: Transfer a known circumference angle through the common tangent and vertically opposite rays, then through the other circle to obtain equal alternate angles.

content.prompt: The two circles in the diagram touch externally at $T$, with common tangent $ATB$ at the point of contact, and $FTP$ and $GTQ$ are straight lines.

spec.description: Externally tangent circles with common tangent ATB and straight FTP/GTQ.
spec.mathematics: Centres(-1,0),(.75,0) and radii1,.75 give exact external tangency at origin. P/Q are negative.75-scaled F/G, so specified line/circle/parallel incidences are exact; apparent GTQ alignment is not an additional marked given.

children.prompt: Let $\angle F=\theta$. Prove that $\angle GTB=\theta$ and $\angle QTA=\theta$.

answer.worked:
In the left circle, $\angle GTB=\angle GFT=\theta$ (alternate segment theorem).

Since $GTQ$ and $ATB$ are straight lines, $\angle QTA=\angle GTB=\theta$ (vertically opposite angles).
In the right circle, $\angle QPT=\angle QTA=\theta$ (alternate segment theorem). Thus $\angle GFT=\angle QPT$. These are equal alternate angles on transversal $FTP$, so $FG\parallel QP$.
